title: windowed quota ghost sampling on edge proxy causing transient overcharge
creator: Maya Chen
description: Customers observed short bursts of apparent token usage (10-30s) that were billed but had no matching inbound requests in our API logs. Investigation traced the source to the edge-side sampling layer which sometimes emitted duplicated samples from a stale sampling window during proxy config reloads. These duplicates flow into the regional aggregator and get counted as additional token usage despite being logically the same request. The bug is constrained to windowed-metering paths behind the edge proxy (edge sampler -> regional aggregator) during rolling config updates and short-lived proxy reconnects.
steps_to_repro: 1) Deploy edge proxy with windowed sampling enabled and an active per-route quota
2) Generate steady single-key traffic (~5 qps) for 2 minutes
3) Trigger a proxy config reload (simulate fleet rollout) causing the sampler to restart and rehydrate state
4) Observe regional aggregator input: some sample batches contain repeated sample IDs for the last 10-30 seconds of traffic
5) Verify billing aggregation shows a temporary spike in token counts that does not correspond to API ingests in upstream request logs
investigation_notes: 02/12: Reproduced locally with a small harness. Root cause appears to be a non-atomic sampler checkpoint write + reconnect: sampler persists last-window checkpoint and then during restart replays in-flight buffers without clearing replay flag.
02/18: Aggregator dedupe is time-window naive — it accepts samples if sample_id missing even when checksum matches. This allows duplicates during short reconnects.

02/22: Confirmed duplicates retain identical request_id and identical token counts; however aggregator attribution logic uses per-sample monotonic counter which can reset on proxy reconnect, creating new distinct sequence ids that still represent same requests.

02/25: Impact analysis: handful of customers saw 2-5% short-lived billing spikes for heavy short-lived bursts. No evidence of long-term double-billing, but downstream invoices include the spiked windows in usage aggregates.
03/01: Cross-check with billing pipeline: billing backfill logic currently trusts aggregator-delivered counts; no downstream dedupe exists at billing level for identical request_id within 60s window.
proposed_fix: 1) Edge-sampler: make checkpoint write + buffer handoff atomic. Add a durable restart flag to avoid replaying the same buffer after restart.
2) Aggregator: add deterministic dedupe using (origin_node_id, request_id, sample_checksum) with TTL of 90s. This will filter duplicates that slip through due to reconnect reorder.
3) Billing pipeline: add a final defensive dedupe pass for identical request_id+timestamp within invoice window as a safety net.
4) Add unit + integration tests for sampler restart scenarios and aggregator-level dedupe effectiveness.
rollout_plan: Phase A (canary): deploy edge-sampler patch to two low-traffic regions and enable aggregator dedupe as opt-in. Monitor token delta and mistakes-dashboard for 48h.
Phase B (ramp): enable aggregator dedupe globally, disable opt-in, keep billing defensive dedupe in place. Monitor for false positives for 7 days.
Phase C (cleanup): after stable 7-day window, remove experimental logging and tighten TTL to 60s if safe. Ship runtime-1.20
Rollback: aggregator dedupe can be disabled remotely via config flag; sampler fix is safe to rollback but may reintroduce duplicates until cleanup path addressed.
qa_criteria: Automated harness reproduces previous duplicate samples and verifies they are filtered post-fix
End-to-end test: no token spikes in billing simulator when sampler restart simulated
No legitimate requests dropped by dedupe for >14 days of canary traffic
PR load test: latency impact from aggregator dedupe < 1% P95
metrics: baseline_duplicate_rate: 0.7% of sampled batches in affected regions
expected_reduction: >99% duplicates removed at aggregator after fix
billing_spike_reduction: reduce transient overcharge windows by >98%
latency_cost: aggregator additional CPU < 3% per shard at peak load
